text:
jamie: Heads up — eu2 warm-pool latency spike 06:12 UTC. Looks like a noisy neighbor on rack-18 (sustained DMA bursts + KV cache churn). link: https://telemetry.redwood/eu2/rack-18 :eyes:

deploy-bot: ALERT: eu2.warmpool.latency > 95p for 10m. Affected tenants: multiple. Triggered runbook 'warm-pool-noise' (INC-8421).

srinivas: I pulled the traces. HBM eviction spikes + PCIe tx queue deepening. Likely large batched attention workload (tenant hypertrain-ops). Any idea if they started a new training sweep?

jamie: hypertrain-ops did a scheduled heavy run at 05:50 UTC. We saw preemptions and spillover to neighboring slots. Their p99 generator tokens/sec jumped 4x.

leah: Can we move them to a dedicated slice? EU2 dedicated spare is basically 0 right now. Option: carve fractional dedicated slices (2 slices) or short-term VLAN/NIC policing to limit burst. Fractional looks cleaner but adds cost ~+$8k/mo. Thoughts?

alex: Short-term mitigation: host-level QoS (nic policing + egress shaping) + soft isolation annotation on the nodes in rack-18. Lower blast radius quickly. I can apply a policy and rate-limit their tenant to 300mbit.

srinivas: Do it. Also prepare a fallback routing rule: route small latency-sensitive requests for affected tenants to US-W quantized pool until saturation eases. Need product approval for cross-region fallback.

jamie: Product is fine with fallback for 1 hour while we stabilize. We should also enable per-tenant DMA burst and kv_cache_evictions metric in the dashboard.

opsbot: Created ticket INF-8421: "eu2 rack-18 noisy neighbor - mitigation and followup". Runbook link: https://redwood.in/inf/8421. Notes:
```
# mitigation steps
kubectl annotate node rack-18 isolation=soft
redwoodctl qos apply --tenant hypertrain-ops --egress 300mbit
redwoodctl route add-fallback --tenant hypertrain-ops --target us-west-quantized --ttl 3600
```

alex: I'll run the mitigation in 5m and post progress. @leah @srinivas please monitor tail-latency after change.

leah: Oncall paged and watching. If tail persists after 20m, we'll escalate to carving fractional slices.

srinivas: Post-mitigation next steps: cost analysis for fractional carveout vs continued shaping + automated detection rule for sustained DMA bursts > 5m. I'll take cost analysis (assign to INF-8421).

jamie: Thanks — if mitigation works, we can close incident and schedule a short retro. If it doesn't, we proceed with fractional carveout. :thumbsup:
